outlooks.summary: Severe storms with a threat for large hail and damaging wind are expected from a portion of the upper Mississippi Valley into the Great Lakes Thursday. Other storms with a few strong wind gusts are possible from the Tennessee Valley to North Carolina and Virginia Thursday afternoon. An isolated severe hail and wind threat will also exist from eastern Wyoming into central Nebraska.

sections.title: Upper MS Valley/Upper Great Lakes
sections.text: Early-morning WV imagery depicts a well-defined short-wave trough topping the western US ridge over SK digging southeast toward the upper MS Valley. Strong convection has developed ahead of this feature near the international border and multiple thunderstorm clusters, or perhaps an MCS, will propagate across northern MN toward the upper Great Lakes early in the day1 period. This activity will be enhanced by a veered LLJ that should translate into WI by 18z. Latest short-range model guidance suggests a pronounced surface front will progress to a position from western Lake Superior, southwest into northwestern IA by mid afternoon. This boundary will likely serve as the focus for renewed thunderstorm development as surface temperatures soar into the lower 90s over southeast MN and extreme western WI. While low-level flow will be decidedly westerly ahead of the front, convective temperatures should be breached across WI into extreme southeast MN and adequate convergence should exist along the front for thunderstorm development. sections.title: High Plains
sections.text: Upper ridge will build over the central Rockies with a dominant high expected near the Four Corners region. As a result, modest northwesterly flow will extend across the northern High Plains which could enhance high-based convection within the upslope regions of trailing cold front from western NE into eastern WY.

sections.title: Mid-South to Middle Atlantic
sections.text: Upper low over the MO Ozark Plateau is weakening and will soon eject into KY, partly in response to upstream height falls over the Great Lakes. A belt of stronger mid-level flow will extend across the TN Valley into the Middle Atlantic along the southern fringe of this deamplifying feature. Convection will continue to exhibit a strong diurnal tendency from the Mid-South into VA and scattered storms will evolve along this corridor by 18z. Gusty winds are the primary threat with any storms that organize within this zone of stronger shear. ..Darrow/Picca.. 07/06/2017

An isolated severe-hail/wind threat extends from southern Nebraska to eastern Wyoming and northeastern Colorado.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The synoptic-scale upper-air pattern continues to amplify and simplify, as a large anticyclone and associated ridging dominate the West, and heights fall across much of eastern Canada and the Great Lakes. A longstanding regime of weak but well-defined troughing from parts of TX to the Ozarks and lower OH Valley region will phase with the Great Lakes troughing. This will occur as the northern part of a shortwave trough -- now evident in moisture-channel imagery from eastern IL across the Ozarks to central/southwest TX -- moves eastward to OH, central KY, western TN and the Arklatex region by 00Z. The weakening remains of this trough should reach PA, the VA/NC Appalachians, and northern MS by the end of the period. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a cold front from far northwestern ON across eastern ND, northwestern SD, to southeastern/central MT. A weak warm front extended from western Lake Superior east-southeastward over the eastern U.P. of Michigan. The cold front will move southward/southeastward today, reaching Lake Superior, northwestern WI, northwestern IA, the NE Sandhills, and western WY by 00Z. outlooks.summary: Severe storms with a threat for large hail and damaging wind are expected from a portion of the upper Mississippi Valley into the Great Lakes today. Other storms with locally damaging wind gusts are possible from the Tennessee Valley to North Carolina and Virginia Thursday afternoon. An isolated severe hail/wind threat also extends from southern Nebraska to eastern Wyoming, northeastern Colorado, and southeast Montana.

sections.title: Upper MS Valley and western Great Lakes
sections.text: This morning's water vapor loop shows a shortwave trough moving across the MN Arrowhead. This feature will continue southwestward this afternoon and aid in the development of afternoon thunderstorms over parts of MN/WI/MI. Surface dewpoints in the mid/upper 60s and strong heating will combine with steep mid level lapse rates to yield strong CAPE values this afternoon. Forecast soundings also show strengthening wind fields through the day, with effective shear becoming favorable for supercell and bowing structures. 12z CAM solutions lack consistency in the location/timing of initiation, but generally agree that intense storms will affect the region later today. Large (potentially very large) hail and damaging winds are the main threats, with some concern for upscale growth and more widespread wind damage this evening as storms move across the ENH area.

sections.title: Gulf Coast states into Mid Atlantic
sections.text: Visible satellite imagery suggests strong heating will occur across a broad corridor from MS to VA today, with low and mid level wind fields slightly stronger than yesterday. It appears likely that pockets of strong instability will develop, promoting scattered afternoon thunderstorms. Larger-scale forcing mechanisms are hard to find, but eventually this region will likely see multiple clusters of storms capable of locally gusty/damaging wind gusts. If these mesoscale areas of greater risk can be identified later today, portions of this corridor will be considered for an upgrade to SLGT risk.

sections.title: MT into NE
sections.text: Widely scattered thunderstorms are expected this afternoon over the northern and central High Plains region, on the east side of a developing upper ridge. The strongest cells in this area may produce hail and gusty winds for a few hours this evening. ..Hart/Mosier.. 07/06/2017

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The overall forecast philosophy from the 1630Z outlook is generally on track, although with a few changes: 1) A couple of linear segments have organized across northern Georgia, and at least one of these segments has produced localized wind damage. This threat will persist into upstate South Carolina a bit south of areas indicated by previous guidance, and there are some indications that this threat will persist even farther downstream into central North Carolina through sunset. 5%/marginal probabilities have been expanded, and a slight risk has been introduced across the Carolinas Piedmont into northern Georgia with the expectation that scattered wind damage/severe wind gusts will occur in these areas. 2) A cluster of storms has developed just northwest of the Arrowhead of Minnesota, and a cumulus field has increase in satellite to the southwest of these storms and very near a surface trough migrating through that region. outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will spread across the upper Great Lakes region tonight, primarily across Wisconsin where damaging winds and large hail are expected. Elsewhere, a few strong storms remain possible across the northern and central High Plains and from the Tennessee Valley to the Middle Atlantic.

sections.title: Upper Great Lakes
sections.text: Heights are beginning to fall across the upper Great Lakes region as troughing establishes itself over southeast Canada into the OH Valley. Within strengthening northwesterly flow, large-scale forcing for ascent appears to be aiding convection across northern WI/U.P. of MI where scattered supercells have evolved over the last few hours. Local radar data suggests large hail is occurring with this activity and 00z soundings from GRB/MPX/DVN all exhibit steep lapse rates supportive of significant hail growth within the most robust updrafts. As deep-layer flow gradually veers convection across northern WI should propagate southeast toward central Lake MI. If a sufficient cold pool develops an MCS may ultimately evolve across this region. Given the reservoir of instability observed across this region the threat of severe should persist late into the evening/early morning hours.

sections.title: Elsewhere
sections.text: A few strong wind gusts/hail may accompany the most robust convection across the High Plains from northeast WY into northwest KS. Isolated strong gusts may also be noted for the next few hours with convection from northern MS into southern VA. ..Darrow.. 07/07/2017

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm coverage will increase through the afternoon with occasionally strong/damaging wind gusts possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Ongoing thunderstorms across the region are expected to persist through the afternoon with additional development possible as heating continues to destabilize the downstream airmass. Estimated storm motion of the line of storms currently moving through eastern TN is 260 at 35-40 kt, taking it to the TN/NC border by 18Z. The areal extent of this line may increase with time as it interacts with development out ahead of it and/or along its flanks. The lack of stronger flow aloft suggests that the widespread damaging wind potential is low but the forward propagating nature of this line will likely result in some strong wind gusts along the leading edge of its outflow. Additionally, water loaded downbursts are possible with the more cellular convection farther south across northeast AL and northern GA, contributing to an isolated damaging wind threat. Uncertainty regarding the overall evolution of the line leads to low watch probabilities but convective trends across the region will be monitored closely for more organization that might require a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated risk for hail/wind may develop as thunderstorms intensify this afternoon as they move southeast across parts of the Upper Great Lakes.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows a small cluster of thunderstorms developing north of the Arrowhead of MN, downstream of a shortwave trough moving from southeastern Manitoba into the Upper Great Lakes. A residual plume of moderately steep 700-500 mb lapse rates (7.1 degrees C/km) on the 12Z INL raob and moderate west-northwesterly flow in the mid- to high-levels will support some storm organization. It is possible additional storms may form to the southwest of the ongoing activity across Ontario. If additional storms develop, a risk for hail/wind may include the Arrowhead of MN and into western parts of the Upper Peninsula later this afternoon. The expected coverage and intensity of storms will likely preclude the need for a severe thunderstorm watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging wind gusts are possible across portions of south-central KY and middle TN as a line of storms this afternoon/evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent regional radar imagery has shown a slight increase in the forward speed of the convective line moving across south-central KY. The downstream airmass over south-central KY and adjacent middle TN is moist and unstable, with recent mesoanalysis estimating MLCAPE around 1000-1500 J/kg. This downstream instability is expected to result in general storm persistence for at least the next few hours with some additional development southward into middle TN possible. Additionally, per the OHX VAD, mid-level flow from 30 to 35 kt exists over the area with some slight increase possible later this afternoon/evening at shortwave trough continues eastward. This kinematic environment is supportive of at least modest storm organization, as evidenced by the organized convective line. Continued forward propagation by the line will result in the potential for strong/damaging wind gusts along the cold pool this afternoon. Anticipated isolated/sporadic nature of the strong wind gusts is expected to preclude the need for a watch but convective trends will be monitored closely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increasing thunderstorm coverage is anticipated with isolated to widely scattered damaging wind gusts possible for the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorm coverage is expected to increase over the next hour or so as subtle forcing for ascent provided by both an approaching shortwave trough and an outflow boundary (associated with earlier convection across middle TN) interact with the warm, moist, and unstable airmass across the Piedmont. Mesoanalysis estimates MLCAPE is currently around 1500 J/kg. Area VAD profiles show modest mid-level flow (i.e. around 20 kt at 6 km) and weak shear, suggesting generally unorganized storms. However, some increase in the mid-level flow is anticipated, supporting the potential for some brief storm organization. Even with the anticipated lack of storm organization, moderate instability within the moist airmass will still support updrafts strong enough for water loading and a resulting threat for damaging downburst winds. Isolated to widely scattered nature of the damaging winds is expected to preclude the need for a watch but convective trends across the region will be monitored closely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will likely intensify this afternoon while moving southeast across the western Lake Superior vicinity and into adjacent portions of WI and MI. Uncertainty remains how thunderstorms will evolve and the overall strength/coverage of strong to severe storm activity.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows a cumulus field beginning to develop across north-central WI east-southeast to the south of the Door Peninsula. Thunderstorms from early-day convection have moved east towards Lake Huron but outflow from this activity spread across northern WI into the western Upper Peninsula. The region within the influence of the outflow is most evident in both the lack of vigorous cumulus growth and drier low levels with surface dewpoints in the upper 50s to lower 60s degrees F. Veered boundary-layer flow (reference deep westerly flow from KDLH and KGRB) has contributed to a lack of strong low-level convergence. Nonetheless, strengthening winds with height (40-60 kt in the 4-8 km layer per KDLH VAD data) will act to organize updrafts. It appears the strongest storms will move southeast along the outflow/buoyancy gradient located from near ASX to GRB. Isolated large hail and isolated to scattered gusts (50-65 mph) capable of wind damage, are possible this evening. Convective trends will be monitored for the possibility of a severe thunderstorm watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging winds and perhaps some hail will remain possible this evening with a cluster of thunderstorms moving slowly southeastward. Watch issuance is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms that developed this afternoon across western NE along a weak surface boundary/wind shift have congealed into a loosely organized cluster across far southwestern NE into northwestern KS over the past hour. Northwesterly mid-level flow around 25-30 kt and a strongly veering wind profile are supporting around 30-35 kt of effective bulk shear and some storm organization. A very well-mixed boundary layer characterized by 40-50 F surface temperature-dewpoint spreads will encourage efficient transfer of convectively enhanced downdraft winds to the surface. Isolated damaging winds should be the main threat with this multicell cluster as it moves southeastward across northwestern KS through the remainder of the evening within a weakly unstable airmass, although some hail may also occur with the strongest cores. The marginal thermodynamic and kinematic environment will likely limit a more robust/widespread severe threat, and watch issuance is not expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for large hail and damaging winds continues across the remaining valid portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 400. A bowing line of severe storms across Door County WI may enter northwest lower Michigan around 0330Z with at least a localized risk for damaging winds. Trends in thunderstorm coverage across central Wisconsin are being monitored however the need for a downstream watch is not immediately evident.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A bowing line of severe storms was moving southeast at 40 kts across the northern Door Peninsula in northeast Wisconsin at 0230Z with a history of marginally severe wind gusts and small hail. As this complex continues southeast in the vicinity of a diffuse northwest-southeast oriented outflow boundary from storms earlier today, some risk for damaging gusts may continue across northwest lower Michigan into the late evening hours. With the onset of nocturnal cooling, some uncertainty remains regarding the potential longevity of this convective line as it moves across northwest lower Michigan within a gradient in MUCAPE, however radar/near-storm environmental trends will continue to be monitored. To the west of the bowing segment, a broken line of strong/occasionally severe thunderstorms extends west to vicinity of Rusk County Wisconsin. In the presence of moderate elevated instability and 35-40 kts of deep-layer shear, the risk for isolated severe storms is expected to continue for at least a couple more hours, aided by ascent with a mid-level impulse moving southeast across the watch area. A third area of severe storms exhibiting supercell characteristics was located over central Wisconsin at 0230Z with a history of large/isolated significant hail. Left split-associated storm mergers have recently resulted in an increase in coverage as the storms move southeast within a moderate-strongly unstable environment and 30-35 kts of deep shear. Latest high-resolution guidance suggests that the severe threat may remain somewhat focused/localized for the next couple of hours, casting some uncertainty on the need for a downstream watch. Radar trends will be monitored for increasing organization of the thunderstorms across southern portions of Wisconsin this evening. ..Bunting.. 07/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Although isolated instances of severe wind and/or hail may continue for a couple more hours, a downstream watch is not anticipated south of the remaining valid counties in Severe Thunderstorm Watch 400.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered strong/occasionally severe storms were in progress across central and southern Wisconsin at 0425Z, with the strongest storms currently south of the watch area northwest of Milwaukee and just north of Madison. Latest objective analysis reveals an environment supportive of a continued risk for isolated strong/severe storms with moderate MUCAPE and 30-35 kts of effective shear. Current radar trends suggest that the overall severe risk will remain isolated and as a result a downstream watch is not currently anticipated. Nevertheless, a couple stronger storms will continue to pose a risk for large hail and damaging wind gusts for at least the next 1-2 hours. ..Bunting.. 07/07/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Locally strong/damaging wind gusts will remain possible into the early morning across portions of southwest into south-central Lower Michigan. WW issuance is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 0710Z, mosaic radar imagery showed a band of storms extending from Kent to Allegan counties, moving to the east-southeast around 50 kt. This band of storms should continue to move to the east-southeast along a moderate instability gradient. At 720Z, GRR WSR-88D velocity data indicated wind speeds of 50-60 kt at 350-400 fl above-radar-level spreading across southwest Kent County. Despite some surface-based inhibition that would limit stronger wind gusts from reaching the surface, reported severe wind gusts with this band of storms and aforementioned kinematics suggest locally strong/damaging wind gusts remain possible into south-central Lower Michigan. Convection/storms developing east of the aforementioned fast-moving band of storms should convectively overturn the downstream air mass and eventually result in a deceleration of the band of storms.
